description:
FILED s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), from the #535 probes.  PRE-EXISTING; named
as such in #535's own text ("the bare-STDOUT unbound form, PRE-EXISTING, aborts
one form on BOTH trees").  #452 fixed `_bareword_fh_p` for the `<FH>` and print
`:fh` slots and #491 did the qualified spellings; THIS site -- the third
argument of a dup open -- was reached by neither.

REPRODUCER:

    use strict;
    my $r = open(my $stdout, ">&", STDOUT);
    print STDERR "ret=", (defined $r ? ($r ? 1 : 0) : "undef"), "\n";

        perl  ret=1     (and `print $stdout "x"` reaches stdout)
        PCL   Unhandled unbound-variable: The variable STDOUT is unbound.

The emitted CL passes the CL symbol STDOUT as a VALUE where a handle DESIGNATOR
is wanted.  The runtime already resolves every designator shape through
%p-resolve-fh (a name string, a glob, a glob ref, a stream, an fd number), so
the fix is on the EMISSION side: a bareword in an argument slot that takes a
filehandle must be emitted the way the builtin path does it -- QUOTED, as a
name -- not as a variable reference.

perl's own t/io/open.t line 258 is the corpus site (`ok( open(my $stdout, ">&",
STDOUT), 'dup STDOUT into lexical fh')`, perl's test 115): it aborts a whole
top-level form there, which is a handful of rows.

BAR: the reproducer for STDOUT/STDERR/STDIN and a user bareword (`open(FOO,...)`
then `open(my $d, ">&", FOO)`), the inverse (a bareword that is NOT a handle
must keep its current meaning), t/io/open.t test 115, and a guard row in
Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t beside the #513 dup rows.  A `Pl/**` change: generation
bump, corpus-diff, emission A/B, full sweep.
subject: A BAREWORD filehandle in the dup SOURCE slot -- open(my $fh, ">&", STDOUT) -- emits a bare CL symbol and dies "The variable STDOUT is unbound" (the site #452 did not reach)
